_doc: Midas verdicts for census-byteoffset.py, round 5 (docs/port-ios/08-round5-census.md). Rules with "src":"donor" are the donor (GoldenEye-Decomp-ios @ 31dc846e) verdicts re-applied to the same merged code and re-read on Midas; "src":"midas" rules are new. Hand verdicts for scripts/census-byteoffset.py (round 19d, D-100). A rule matches a row when its file equals the row's file and its regex matches the row's source line (or the N64-arm match text); 'kind' optionally restricts to CAST/PUN/COPY/ALLOC/STORAGE/N64ARM. First match wins. Mechanical verdicts (SAME by identical layout or identical field, NOT-ACCESS) need no rule.

rules.why: D290 (upstream a5804d1, D-139): the N64 copy spans D_80035D04's last word into watchControllerButtonBases, the ModelRenderData template (zbufferenabled=TRUE, flags=3); the PORT arm builds the explicit template, as at the D264 site

`offset += 8` is the N64 sizeof(bg_portal_data_entry); the host entry is 16 (`bg_portal_entry *` first), so every portal after [0] is read at the wrong stride. Unreferenced function (sub_GAME_7F0B8DF4). Fixed: index by element.
D-100: indexed by element

only ever dereferenced at offset 0 (`*rwdata = ...`): the Switch record's `visible` word

the pointer escapes to chraction.c, which reads `unk2c[3]` = N64 byte 0xc = angle_offset; on the host byte 0xc is turn_angle_per_frame (the union `anim` is 8 bytes). Fixed by typing the field
a file offset from the setup file added to the HOST file base (the converted file's own layout)

arg1 is a weapon_firing_animation_table *: N64 [12],[13],[16],[17] = max_up, max_down, free_arm_frac_up, free_arm_frac_down; host bytes 0x30/0x34/0x40/0x44 = aim_end_frame, max_up, max_right, free_arm_frac_up (the union `anim` is 8 bytes). Every armed guard's aim-pitch clamp and off-arm follow fraction
pointer difference in host bytes, consumed as host bytes

image_entry byte 0 & 0xf: on the N64 (MSB-first bitfields, decomp IMAGE() = {HS, HT, SZ}) it is hitTexture; on the host the PORT struct puts dataoffset in bits 0-23, so it is the low nibble of the texture's ROM offset -- a pseudo-random hit type 0..15 against a 13-entry table. Upstream's D67 note claims the N64 reads dataoffset here; it does not (byte 0 is the MSB on a big-endian word)
a Gfx buffer used as a raw load buffer (bytes in, bytes out)

callee reads arg0[2] & 3: N64 byte 8..11 BE, low two bits = tex->depth; host byte 8 is the low word of `u8 *data`, so depth reads as the pointer's alignment bits (0) and the G_LOADBLOCK dxt is computed for 4-bit texels. fast3d ignores dxt, so no visible change; the GBI word does change
